scores.visual_critic_note: Muted Tableau10 palette and dark organic edge bundles show intentionality, but the visualization is cropped in the viewport, the controls row is utilitarian developer-UI (FPS counter, easing params), and the blue active-button vs green action-button color conflict undermines the otherwise cohesive palette.
scores.encoding_integrity_note: Correct scaleSqrt for force-layout node sizing and keyed data joins throughout, but the sunburst y-scale applies a redundant sqrt to uniform depth values, mildly distorting perceived hierarchy depth without clear justification.
scores.stress_test_note: The dominant flaw is the un-throttled easing-param sliders each triggering a full 1500ms layout transition on every mousemove, a textbook Update Storm; the visualization is otherwise clean with no feedback loops and correct scale closure usage.
scores.cognitive_load_note: Color groupings and hierarchical clustering are clear, but 300 bundled edges at low tension converge into an unreadable central hairball, and simultaneous animation of 200+ nodes across 8 layout morphs poses congruence risk not assessable from the static screenshot.
flags: Update Storm: easing-params sliders (amplitude, period, overshoot) fire full updateLayout() on every input event with no debounce or RAF coalescing, triggering a 1500ms transition recalculation per pixel of slider movement

Mid-Flight Snap: no explicit .interrupt() call before creating new svg.transition(); relies on D3 implicit cancellation, leaving d.current_x/d.current_y in mid-interpolation state if the tween render tick hasn't yet committed — the .on('end') state sync is never reached on interrupt
Mouse-Touch Fight: force-simulation drag and node click/hover attach no touch filtering (no event.sourceEvent checks, no pointer-event deduplication), risking ghost interactions on touch devices

proposer:
820 lines, down from 827 (-7 lines). Changes:
